proposed_protocol: Use the complete acquired thorax with contiguous thin sections at most 1.5 mm, typically 1 mm, and explicit coverage/quality limitations. Record acquired thickness separately from reconstruction interval and pixel spacing.
Use suitable lung windows and actual multiplanar reconstructions to distinguish nodule/linear scar and solid/subsolid components; retain the actual source reconstructions and kernel.
Measure verified fat or calcium on the thinnest available nonsharpened series with a small ROI, excluding air/edge partial-volume contamination. A single point value is insufficient.

Compare all available original prior studies, including early baseline; document dates, reconstruction/software compatibility and uncertainty. A current source example is not an invented prior examination.

Declare incidental/screening/oncology/infectious context, eligibility and exclusions before applying a named current guideline. Distinguish single/multiple and solid/pure-ground-glass/part-solid pathways.

Document each nodule ID/site/series/image, total/solid-component measurement, margins, verified fat/calcification, relevant pleural/airway/vascular relationships and actual interval change. Reader scores are not histological diagnoses.

proposed_walkthrough_steps.label: Assessment and recommendation
proposed_walkthrough_steps.detail: Identify the most suspicious nodule and give a recommendation with the guideline and its rationale.
findings: For an eligible incidental solitary solid nodule under 6 mm: no routine follow-up at low risk; optional 12 month CT at high risk, adjusted for morphology/context.
For an eligible incidental solitary solid 6–8 mm nodule: initial CT 6–12 months; later 18–24 month assessment depends on risk and stability.
For qualifying multiple solid nodules with at least one 6 mm nodule: initial CT 3–6 months; assess the most suspicious nodule and the applicable later follow-up branch.
For qualifying solitary pure ground-glass nodules at least 6 mm: initial CT 6–12 months, then every 2 years until 5 years if persistent and appropriate.
For qualifying solitary part-solid nodules at least 6 mm overall: initial CT 3–6 months; persistent dense-component size, growth and morphology can warrant further evaluation.
Screening, known malignancy, immunocompromise, young adults and alternative causes require their actual pathway; do not combine Fleischner/BTS/Lung-RADS thresholds.
proposed_walkthrough_steps.look: Apply the chosen guideline to the most suspicious nodule.
